key_insight: LLMs labeled incidental findings in lung cancer screening CT reports with moderate to almost perfect agreement, but no model–prompt combination performed best across all nine findings.
clinical_relevance: This report-labeling research could support incidental-finding data extraction in lung cancer screening; it did not evaluate cancer drug discovery or patient outcomes.
method: Retrospective analysis of 300 CT reports from one Dutch academic hospital.
Compared GPT-5, GPT-4-Turbo, Llama-3.1-8B-INST, MedGemma-4B-IT, and keyword search against radiologist labels.
Tested four prompting strategies per LLM, with and without chain-of-thought.
evidence_signal: GPT-5 achieved Cohen’s κ of 0.71–0.97 for seven findings; the highest reported agreement for interstitial lung abnormalities and mediastinal mass was moderate (κ=0.48 and 0.42, respectively), and non-chain-of-thought prompts performed best for most findings.
watch_item: The small, single-center retrospective dataset limits generalizability; broader validation is needed before clinical implementation.
paper_title: Large Language Models to Label CT Radiology Reports for Incidental Findings Found in Lung Cancer Screening: A Comparative Analysis
